title: What is the difference between map() and reduce() in streams?
shortTitle: map() vs reduce(): transformation vs aggregation
keyPoints: map is an intermediate operation that transforms each element independently: N elements in, N elements out.
reduce is a terminal operation that aggregates all elements into a single value: N elements in, 1 value out.
map is lazy and does not trigger execution; reduce is eager and triggers the entire pipeline.
reduce with identity (e.g., BigDecimal.ZERO) always returns a value; without identity it returns Optional.
map+reduce is the fundamental stream paradigm: map shapes the data, reduce summarises it.
For parallel streams, the reduce accumulator must be associative to guarantee correct results.
For complex aggregations like grouping, use collect with Collectors instead of reduce.

s1_definition.oneliner: map transforms each element one-to-one (N to N, intermediate, lazy); reduce aggregates all elements into one value (N to 1, terminal, eager): map shapes data, reduce summarises it.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **map(Function<T,R>)**: intermediate, lazy. Transforms each element independently. Same count, different type/value.
- **reduce(identity, BinaryOperator)**: terminal, eager. Folds all elements into one value. Triggers pipeline.
- **reduce without identity**: returns Optional to handle empty streams.
- **Three forms of reduce**: (1) `reduce(BinaryOperator) -> Optional<T>`, (2) `reduce(identity, BinaryOperator) -> T`, (3) `reduce(identity, BiFunction, BinaryOperator) -> U` for parallel.
- **map+reduce pattern**: the fundamental stream paradigm, mirroring the MapReduce programming model.
s1_definition.analogy: map is the currency exchange counter at National Bank of India: each dollar cheque becomes a rupee cheque. 100 cheques in, 100 cheques out. reduce is the adding machine: 100 cheque amounts go in, one total comes out. Together: map converts all cheques to rupees (transformation), then reduce adds all rupee amounts into one grand total (aggregation).

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  map+reduce pattern:
  ─────────────────────
  [TXN-001, TXN-002, TXN-003]     Source (3 elements)
       │
  map(Transaction::amount)
       │
  [45000, 78000, 120000]           Transformed (3 elements)
       │
  reduce(ZERO, BigDecimal::add)
       │
  243000                            Aggregated (1 value)

  map: N elements → N elements (transform)
  reduce: N elements → 1 value (aggregate)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
map and reduce are fundamentally different operations that work together. map is an intermediate operation that transforms each element: N elements in, N elements out. reduce is a terminal operation that aggregates all elements into one value: N elements in, 1 value out.

The map+reduce pattern is the fundamental stream paradigm: map shapes the data into the right form, reduce summarises it into the final answer. For complex aggregations, use collect with Collectors instead of reduce.

Remember one sentence: map transforms N elements to N elements, reduce folds N elements into 1 value, and together they form the fundamental stream pattern.
